module purpose: neorv32_fifo is a parameterizable FIFO buffer that optionally qualifies write and read requests with free/avail status, stores incoming wdata_i words in fifo_reg or fifo_mem, returns the selected stored word on rdata_o, and reports queue occupancy and threshold status on level_o, free_o, avail_o, and half_o.

use-case flows.value: accepted write request that enables a FIFO write and write-pointer advance
accepted read request that enables a read-pointer advance
input FIFO payload word written into fifo_reg or fifo_mem on an accepted write
stored FIFO payload word returned on rdata_o from fifo_reg or from the selected fifo_mem entry
FIFO occupancy count and free/data-available/half-full status
queue state cleared to zero by rstn_i or clear_i, with optional storage and sync-status reset depending on generics

conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes the write-accept decision in `we <= we_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (we_i and free);` at line 65. That decision controls write-pointer progression in line 82 and gates payload storage in lines 134-150 and 170-184. Integrity is established because a wrong decision writes data or advances the write side contrary to the RTL-defined qualification. Availability is also established: when this decision is true and a rising edge occurs, the selected storage element captures the input word and `w_pnt` updates at line 76.

The module computes the read-accept decision in `re <= re_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (re_i and avail);` at line 64. That decision controls read-pointer progression in line 83, updates the asynchronous read pointer copy at line 210, and therefore determines which queued entry is exposed by the read path at line 213 or line 241. Integrity is established because a wrong decision advances or suppresses dequeue state contrary to the RTL-defined qualification, which changes subsequent read order and reported occupancy. Availability is also established: when this decision is true and a rising edge occurs, `r_pnt` updates at line 77 so the read path can progress.

The payload write flow stores `wdata_i` into `fifo_reg` in the depth-1 build (lines 135 or 171) or into `fifo_mem` at the addressed slot in larger builds (lines 150 or 184). The read-out flow returns `fifo_reg` directly at lines 201 or 232, or a selected `fifo_mem` entry at lines 213 or 241, depending on `fifo_depth_c` and `FIFO_RSYNC`. Integrity is established because the read-out flow must deliver exactly the stored word from the addressed queue entry. Availability is established conditionally from the RTL: the word is held in `fifo_reg` or `fifo_mem` until queue state changes by later operations or reset/clear behavior, and the configured read path presents it on `rdata_o`. Under `FULL_RESET`, storage is explicitly cleared by `rstn_i` at lines 131-147.

`w_pnt` and `r_pnt` hold the persistent queue position state: lines 76-77 load `w_nxt` and `r_nxt`, while lines 82-83 either clear them to zero, increment them on accepted write/read, or hold their previous values. `w_pnt` selects the write location in lines 150 and 184; `r_pnt` is compared with `w_pnt` to derive occupancy at lines 92-95 or 102-105, and in synchronous read mode selects the returned entry at line 241. In asynchronous read mode, `r_nxt` is copied into `r_pnt_ff` at line 210 only for the read path. Integrity is established because corrupt queue-position state misaddresses storage, breaks FIFO ordering, and corrupts occupancy computation. Availability is established because this state is held in registers and reset to a known zero state by `rstn_i` at lines 72-75 or by `clear_i` through lines 82-83.

The module computes occupancy status from the pointer state. In larger FIFOs, `level <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt));` at line 95, `half <= level(level'left-1) or full;` at line 96, and `full`/`empty` are derived from pointer comparisons at lines 92-94. In the single-entry build, lines 102-106 derive `full`, `empty`, `level`, and `half` from `match`. `free <= not full;` and `avail <= not empty;` at lines 110-111. The report flow drives `level_o` at lines 116-117 and drives `free_o`, `avail_o`, and `half_o` either directly at lines 217-219 or through the synchronous status registers at lines 249-256. When `FIFO_SAFE` is true, `free` and `avail` also qualify the accepted write and read decisions at lines 65 and 64. Integrity is established because both the reported status and optional safe acceptance depend on these exact decisions and counts. Availability is established because the outputs are driven in every read-mode configuration, with synchronous status outputs reset to zero by `rstn_i` at lines 249-252.
